title: Traffic contingency scenarios and risk-weighted milestone plan for feature experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a formal traffic contingency matrix and a risk-weighted milestone plan that lets PMs and SREs run A/B tests and canaries with deterministic escalation and rollback behavior. Scope includes: definition of ramp windows and stat windows, primary + secondary metric baskets, quantified risk buckets (low/medium/high) tied to traffic caps, automated mitigation actions (shift-to-fallback, degrade feature, full rollback), required instrumentation and dashboards, and handoff/runbook artifacts for on-call.

Background: recent experiments revealed ambiguous thresholds and manual escalation steps that caused inconsistent rollbacks and customer-visible regressions. This ticket captures a template and the accompanying instrumentation checklist so teams can run repeatable, auditable experiments across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Proposal summary:
- Create a traffic contingency matrix mapping observed metric breach patterns to actions (throttle %, degrade, rollback). Each row is a risk bucket with a recommended action and an owner.
- Define risk-weighted milestones across the experiment lifecycle: "init smoke" (0-1% traffic), "confidence ramp" (1-20%), "scale hold" (20-60%), "full roll" (60-100%). Each milestone has hard/soft thresholds and a minimum evaluation window.
- Specify the statistical evaluation windows (min N requests, minimum time) and suggested AB test analysis method for short-tail metrics (use bootstrap CI on latency percentiles) and long-tail metrics (time-series anomaly detection with control charts).
- Instrumentation checklist: metric coverage (primary metric + 4 secondaries), alert wiring (PagerDuty escalation), dashboards (per-model/per-route), and retention for experiment datasets (14 days by default; 90 days for enterprise customers).
- Runbook: step-by-step play for each contingency: who to page, which toggles in Console to change, how to adjust routing policies, and post-mortem requirements.

Success criteria: standard template adopted by 3 product teams during the next cycle and one cross-team oncall fire drill to validate automation paths.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable traffic contingency matrix doc lives in Confluence and is linked from the experiment PR template
Instrumented dashboards exist for latency P50/P95, error rate, cost-per-token, and quality regression signal for the first experiment using the template
Automated canary throttle toggle implemented in Console (ability to set emergency throttle to 5/10/25/50%) with audit log entries
Two simulated fault drills executed with SRE and Product owning the playbook and notes captured
Template adopted by at least three product teams in the cycle (tracked via PRs referencing PM-88321)
comments: 2026-02-18 — Aisha Patel: Drafted the initial contingency matrix and posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/experiments/contingency-matrix. Holding the doc open for feedback from SRE and Analytics.

2026-02-22 — Marco Rivera: Reviewed matrix; suggested separating quality-signal alerts (semantic regressions) from infra signals (latency/errors). Added a 'quality' risk bucket and recommended a separate pager path to LLM QA.

2026-02-27 — Priya Kulkarni (SRE): Raised concern about automated throttle binary toggles — proposed gradual throttles (5->10->25) rather than single-step to avoid oscillation. Added instrumentation requirement to verify circuit-breaker hysteresis.

2026-03-03 — Data Infra (notes): Created a query template for experiment cohorts and recommended minimum sample sizes. Linked draft analysis notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/experiment-analysis/pulls/92

2026-03-09 — Marco Rivera: Coordinated with Console eng to add an 'emergency throttle' control in the staging console; eng requested a small API contract change (ENG-23177). Marking follow-up dependency below.
decision_log: 2026-02-20 — Decision: Use a separate 'quality' pager route for semantic/regression signals to avoid noisy infra pages (approved by SRE and Product)
2026-02-25 — Decision: Default experiment data retention set to 14 days; enterprise experiments can opt for 90 days (trade-off: cost vs auditability)
2026-03-04 — Decision: Implement staggered throttle (5%, then 10%, then 25%) as the default automated mitigation to reduce risk of oscillation (agreed with SRE)
2026-03-08 — Decision: Require a canary 'hold' of minimum 24 hours or 10k requests per milestone before any automatic scale up
postmortem_requirements: Timeline with exact traffic percentages and timestamps
Metric deltas vs control and a short causal hypothesis
Action items and owners within 48 hours
